clue.text: Old fellow arranged to be with a person during time held up without a home

indicators.note: during says the arranged-person stretch sits inside the time word
held up in a down clue means the time word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an eon is a very long period of time
something arranged has been fixed, as a match or a date
bod is informal British slang for a person

explanation.surface: A muddled account of an old man and someone else, stuck for a while with nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' only works in a down clue, where the reversed time word reads upward; 'during' wraps it round the rest. BOD is informal British for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the police and press formula for someone with no permanent address, a homeless person.

clue.text: Breather from running nullified on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that lets you breathe is cancelled out by running, seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals letters taken from inside the words: GNUL spans runninG NULlified, and 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing organ is literally a breather, a cryptic but fair description of the respiratory organ.

clue.text: Very sentimental daughter jumping out of river

indicators.note: jumping out of says the daughter letter leaves the river's name

parts.note: the Tweed is a river on the border of Scotland and England
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A soppy girl leaps out of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for excessively sweet, quaint or sentimental.

clue.text: Office employee still getting uppity about a boy

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the a-plus-boy pair
uppity read literally as going up, in a down clue the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: still in the sense of yet, as in still waiting
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A clerk is still becoming arrogant towards a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' looks like an adjective about attitude, but in a down clue it literally means written upwards; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who brought round the tea trolley was a fixture of British offices, an office worker of old.

clue.text: Fair source of sprays etc?

parts.note: fair hints at a young woman (as in My Fair Lady's Eliza Doolittle), and sprays are small bunches of blooms she might sell on the street

explanation.surface: A question about where sprays come from at a fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a funfair but stands for a fair maiden; sprays look like aerosols but are posies.
explanation.definitionFit: A street seller of posies, like Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion, supplies sprays of blooms.

clue.text: Trio at bar getting disorderly — right for one to intervene judiciously?

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters of trio at bar are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Three drinkers become rowdy, so someone fair-minded must step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting disorderly' scrambles the trio's letters; 'for' is a link, and the question mark flags that intervening describes the role only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is appointed to settle a dispute impartially, stepping in with judgement.

clue.text: After breakdown, rev woeful hired vehicle

indicators.note: a breakdown leaves things in pieces, so the words rev woeful hired are reassembled

explanation.surface: After the car breaks down, you rev the miserable rental.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with power to all four wheels is a type of vehicle, often an off-roader.

clue.text: Creative result from one in a scrape with others?

definitions.text: Creative result from one in a scrape with others?

parts.words: Creative result from one in a scrape with others?
parts.note: a scrape suggests trouble, but here it is the scraping of a bow on strings, a soloist playing with an orchestra

explanation.surface: Something inventive comes out of a person in trouble alongside friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow and scrape' is a jokey phrase for string players; the soloist plays with the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for a solo string player accompanied by an orchestra fits this playful description.

clue.text: Pine by hill starts to overshadow wood for poet

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a fell is a hill, especially in northern England

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: A pine tree by a hillside begins to shade the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of The Song of Hiawatha.

clue.text: Appropriate amount of laughter

definitions.meaning: a sudden burst, as in a ... of the giggles

explanation.definitionFit: Means suitable as an adjective, and a sudden outburst, as of laughter, as a noun.

clue.text: Decrease inflexible element in club

definitions.meaning: read as de-crease, to remove creases from clothes
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrease' is cryptic: split it as de-crease, to smooth out creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Means pressing creases out, unbending, the metal Fe, and a golf club.

clue.text: Take in celebrity magazine bar cover

indicators.note: bar means except, and the cover is the first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Heat is a British celebrity gossip weekly

explanation.surface: Absorb a gossip magazine except for its front cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to consume it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A drifter's injured around island? I could be needed!

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the island letter
injured says the letters of a drifter's are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wanderer is hurt near an island, and someone shouts that help may be required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges ADRIFTERS, which goes 'around' I; the injury in the surface is why such help is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trained in emergency treatment speaks here, saying they might be called upon after an injury.

clue.text: Methodical teams City's deployed

indicators.note: deployed says the letters of teams City's are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: City's teams are organised in a careful, orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Done according to a system means orderly and methodical, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A large smoker's resource seen around back of inn in event around the clock?

indicators.note: seen around says the smoker's item surrounds the final letter of inn

parts.note: a lighter is what a smoker uses to light up

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of inn

explanation.surface: A big smoker's supply is spotted around the rear of a pub during a night-long gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A session lasting through the whole night, such as a party or study marathon, goes round the clock.

clue.text: Check report of time in power

indicators.note: report of says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their time in power

explanation.surface: Verify news of how long a ruler held office.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse is to restrain it, so to check is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Live in front of a filthy place round lake? That's vile

indicators.note: in front of places the live word before the rest

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: round says the filthy place surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a byword for a dirty place

explanation.surface: Dwelling outside a disgusting spot near a lake is repulsive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty or horrible: an adjective of strong distaste matching vile.

clue.text: Diplomatic activity following port order to quell trouble

indicators.note: following puts the diplomacy word after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
tact is skill in handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: Diplomacy follows a port authority's command to stop unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading someone this statute was a warning to disperse a mob; idiomatically, a stern telling-off.

clue.text: Criticism curtailed by ambassador — or other member of embassy?

indicators.note: curtailed means the last letter is cut off the criticism word

parts.note: an attack is a strong verbal criticism
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Criticism is cut short by the ambassador or another embassy official.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic staff member with a specialist role is posted to an embassy alongside the ambassador.

clue.text: Leaving sun, disturb fish

indicators.note: leaving says the sun letter departs from the disturb word

parts.note: to shake someone up is to disturb them
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Getting out of the sun upsets a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A white sea fish of the cod family, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: I indulge in tirade about retired group in North-East — being this?

indicators.note: in says the reversed group word sits inside the compass letters

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for North-East

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the group word is read reversed

parts.note: a lot is a group or set, as in that lot
to rant is to deliver a tirade

explanation.surface: Someone admits ranting about pensioners in the North-East, then asks what this makes them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns LOT into TOL, which goes 'in' NE; 'about' is a link to the rest. The definition points back at the speaker of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rails against a group shows narrow-minded bigotry, which is what the speaker is being.

clue.text: Bird beginning to evade foreign character

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of evade

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A bird starts to dodge an exotic figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless Australian bird, so a straightforward example of a bird.

clue.text: Face fool

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a person's face and also for a gullible dupe.

clue.text: End of work — commuter initially meets bother on the way back

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of commuter
on the way back says the bother word is read in reverse

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: At the end of the working day a commuter runs into trouble going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns ADO into ODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing passage of a musical piece, so the end of a work.

clue.text: Care taken about poster with old racing driver subject to recruitment

indicators.note: taken about says the care word goes round the poster and driver

parts.note: to take heed is to take care
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster
James Hunt was a 1976 Formula One world champion

explanation.surface: Careful handling of a poster with a retired racing driver, who is being recruited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' is the container signal; Hunt, a British Formula One champion of the 1970s, is a stock crossword driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Being approached by a recruiting firm for a job means being targeted for recruitment.

clue.text: Confidence shown by comic actor

definitions.meaning: an expectation or trust that things will turn out well
A British-born American comedian and film actor

explanation.definitionFit: Means trust in the future, and is the surname of the comedian Bob, famous for road films.

clue.text: Expose as a lie Nationalist trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A political untruth is shown up amid nationalist unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a lie is an idiom for exposing it as false.

clue.text: Criminal behind top site around Spain? It's irrelevant

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the Spain letter
criminal used loosely as wrong, so the letters of behind top site go wrong

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A crook lurking behind a premier site near Spain is waved away as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Not pertinent to the matter in hand, an idiom meaning irrelevant.
